deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is page 4 of a printed German antiquarian bookseller's catalogue, section 'Naturwissenschaft und Physik'. It continues the section from page 3 and runs on to page 5. The entries are alphabetical, from Becher, J. J. through Büffon. Each entry gives author, short title, format (8., 4., Fol.), place and year (with the leading 1 dropped, e.g. 'Lpzg. 805' = Leipzig 1805), binding (Ppbd., Hlbldrbd., br., etc.), an original price in parentheses in Thaler, and an offered price in Thaler and Silbergroschen (Sgr.). There are no handwritten annotations, formulas, calculations or marginalia by Riemann or anyone else. Dating: the latest imprint here is Bothe, 'Braunschw. 860' (1860). The next page lists Crüger, 'Erl. 1862'. So the catalogue was printed in or after 1862. That is well after the 1853 suggested by the bundle name, though still within Riemann's lifetime. The sheet may be an inserted or mis-filed printed leaf, possibly reused as scrap paper (the reverse side might carry notes), but this side has nothing to reconstruct.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed book-sale catalogue of natural science and physics titles with no mathematical content and no manuscript notes. The only point of mild archival interest is that it dates to about 1862 or later despite the bundle label '1853'.
transcription_corrections: The price unit rendered '₰' is the Thaler sign (ℛ, as in the previous page's transcription), not the pfennig sign.
Becher entry: 'Ber[?]. 674' is most likely 'Berol. 674' (Berlin 1674), where Elsholtz's Destillatoria curiosa was printed.
Bräunlich entry: '2c.' is the Fraktur abbreviation 'zc.' / '&c.' (etc.).
'Borchart, S.' is printed as such but refers to Samuel Bochart's Hierozoicon.
'Spaltanzani' (for Spallanzani) and 'philsos' are misprints in the original, not OCR errors.
Bonnet entry: 'J. A. E. Goeze' is correct for the translator Johann August Ephraim Goeze.
